clue.text: Viceroy prepared to meet scholar

parts.note: to be prepared to do something is to be willing
a don is a university teacher, a scholar

explanation.surface: A Viceroy of India, all set to have a meeting with an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Willingdon was Viceroy of India from 1931 to 1936.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marquess of Willingdon held the post of Governor-General and Viceroy of India.

clue.text: Damage — that's odd in the casino !

explanation.surface: Gamblers note the harm done when the roulette ball lands on an odd number.
explanation.walkthrough: In French roulette 'impair' is the bet on odd numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To harm something is to weaken it; in roulette's French terms, the odd-number bet bears this name.

clue.text: The other kind of clue is in the French game

indicators.note: is in says the clue type sits inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
this clue is a down clue, so the other kind is an across clue

explanation.surface: A puzzle clue of the other sort appears in a French sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to itself: it sits among the down clues, so 'the other kind' is the across sort, set inside the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Appoint about four, in this case

indicators.note: about means around, so the appointing word goes around four

parts.note: to nominate is to appoint someone to a role
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Naming roughly four people for the job, in this instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the grammatical case of a sentence's subject; 'this case' sounds like 'in this instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the subject of a verb takes the nominative case.

clue.text: Lover of Byron's poetry

explanation.surface: A romantic admirer of the poetry of Lord Byron.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Juan is the legendary seducer and the title of Byron's long satirical poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary seducer's name stands for any womanising suitor, and Byron wrote an epic poem titled after him.

clue.text: Close part of 'one area

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Shutting off one section of a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Near and close both mean at a short distance.

clue.text: Strong port ours, perhaps

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible version of ours, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A robust port wine that may be ours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts towards the fortified wine, but it is a Spanish harbour town; 'perhaps' scrambles the possessive word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigorous means full of strength and energy.

clue.text: Pictures the star seldom makes

indicators.note: makes says the letters of the words are made into something new

explanation.surface: Films that the celebrity rarely appears in.
explanation.walkthrough: STAR and SELDOM are rearranged together; 'Pictures' suggests films, but means paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Old masters are paintings by great European artists from before about 1800.

clue.text: Spying 'mince pies, takes a pound

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the letters of pies are chopped and rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone snooping on the Christmas mince pies, which cost a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks like part of the Christmas treat 'mince pies', but it is the signal to scramble the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old noun for the act of spying or catching sight of something.

clue.text: Example of gamble with mine output

parts.note: a spec is a speculation, a gamble

indicators.note: the word mine is put out in a new order, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A risky venture in mining, judged by what the mine produces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'output' reads as what the mine produces, but it signals the four letters of that word coming out rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a sample or instance taken as typical of its kind.

clue.text: King could hold a couple of magnums

definitions.text: could hold a couple of magnums

explanation.surface: A monarch with a thirst big enough for two large bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeroboam was a king of Israel in the Bible; a jeroboam bottle holds four standard bottles, the same as two magnums.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical ruler of Israel gives his name to a wine bottle of four normal bottles' capacity, twice a magnum.

clue.text: A jolly quarter, of which Virgil sang

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
S, south, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A cheerful section of the Aeneid, sung by Virgil.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aeneid opens 'Arma virumque cano', 'Of weapons and the man I sing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's epic begins by announcing its subject as weapons and a man, so weaponry is what he sang of.

clue.text: Arrogance — like taking part of the car into pieces

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
the sump is the oil reservoir under a car's engine

indicators.note: into pieces says the word into is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Smugness, like dismantling a car engine bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' rearranges INTO into TION at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumption can mean presumptuous behaviour, taking too much upon oneself.

clue.text: Put in charge in a different setting, appears greedy

indicators.note: the letters are given a new arrangement, set out differently

parts.note: vicarious authority is delegated, given to someone acting in another's place

explanation.surface: Someone given a position of authority in new surroundings shows a grasping nature.
explanation.walkthrough: VICARIOUS, rearranged by 'different setting', follows A to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaricious describes someone with an excessive craving for money or wealth.

clue.text: Emergency food for anaemia ?

explanation.surface: Survival rations, or a treatment for a blood deficiency.
explanation.walkthrough: An iron ration is a soldier's emergency pack; read literally, a measured dose of iron is what anaemia needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers carried a small emergency food pack by that name, and an iron-deficient patient needs a portion of the metal.

clue.text: Point to Spain and Portugal as Asian territory

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
the Iberian peninsula holds Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Pointing out Spain and Portugal on a map of Asian lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is the vast northern region of Russia lying in Asia.

clue.text: Knight sees girl in French headgear

indicators.note: in puts the girl's name inside the French cap

parts.note: a beret is a soft round cap associated with France
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A knight catches sight of a girl wearing a beret.
explanation.definitionFit: A banneret was a medieval knight entitled to lead men under his own banner.

clue.text: Include minerals in charge, as palmist might do

indicators.note: the instruction to include asks for one piece to be placed within another
in says the minerals go inside the word for a charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
ores are minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: Billing for minerals as part of a fee, as a fortune-teller might.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm reader claims to see the future in the lines of a hand.

clue.text: Trespass, or chance to do it by mistake

indicators.note: a mistake jumbles the letters, so they come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Trespassing, or getting the chance to do so accidentally.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude on another's land or rights.

clue.text: Print plate of gun No. 100 the Italian style

parts.note: the Sten was a British sub-machine gun
C is 100 in Roman numerals
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: A printing plate for a gun numbered 100, made in the Italian manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut sheet through which ink is pressed to print a design.

clue.text: City centre — sham restoration

indicators.note: restoring here means rebuilding the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A town centre given a fake makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restoration' rearranges CENTRE and SHAM together.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester is a large city in north-west England.

clue.text: A way to account for return of spiteful people

indicators.note: return asks for the two pieces to be read backwards

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A method for explaining why nasty folk come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns ST and AC together into CA and TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat is old slang for a spiteful, malicious person, usually a gossiping woman.

clue.text: Slavery to a merciless lady

explanation.surface: Bondage to a cruel woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's ballad 'La Belle Dame sans Merci' ends with the knight in thrall to the beautiful lady without mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrall means bondage, and Keats's knight is held captive by the beautiful lady without pity.

clue.text: Actor replaced by Pat Hines

indicators.note: the letters are placed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A performer whose role has been taken over by someone named Pat Hines.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespian, after Thespis of ancient Greece, means a stage performer.

clue.text: Likewise it's listed

explanation.surface: The same applies to whatever is on the list.
explanation.walkthrough: Item is Latin for 'likewise', once used to introduce each entry in a list.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin adverb meaning also or in the same way, and an entry on an inventory.

clue.text: Ball given by a native

explanation.surface: A dance thrown by a local.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a chinaman is a left-arm bowler's wrist-spun delivery; the second sense is a dated, now offensive term for a native of China.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket names a left-arm wrist-spin delivery this way, and the word once meant a person from China.

clue.text: Love compact in Denmark?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
compact means packed tight, dense

explanation.surface: A romantic agreement made by Danes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compact' looks like a noun, an agreement, but supplies an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Odense is a city on the island of Funen in Denmark.

clue.text: McLean upset saintly follower — dejection results

indicators.note: the saintly word follows the rearranged name
upset means knocked over, the letters overturned into a new order

parts.note: saintly means holy

explanation.surface: A man named McLean, distressed by a religious disciple, ends up downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follower' reads as a disciple of a saint, but it only says the saintly word comes after the scrambled surname, upset by 'upset'.
explanation.definitionFit: Melancholy is a deep, lasting sadness or gloom.
